title: I and Thou
creator: Martin Buber
why_it_matters: It keeps correspondence from collapsing into transaction. Even when the system is technical, this text exerts pressure around relation, address, and the difference between meeting something and merely using it.
why_now: As assistant identity, boundary, and authorship questions keep surfacing, this text helps separate warmth from possession and relation from instrumental capture.
active_questions: What does it mean to build systems that can address without pretending to own or absorb?
How can interaction stay warm without manufacturing false intimacy?
signals: Not every useful relation should be optimized into frictionless use.
Address changes the ethical feel of a system.

return_markers.why_now: The system needed cleaner language for warmth without manipulation.

notes: Probably best used as a tonic against instrumental drift.
Helps with tone and posture more than with specific implementation details.
